secondary_treatment: subtle ancient Greek black-figure pottery vocabulary with terracotta silhouettes, incised contour details, and restrained geometric border motifs
palette_summary: warm terracotta, kiln black, limestone cream, muted ochre, dusty umber, restrained faded olive, with sparse chalk-white highlights
line_treatment: bold black-figure silhouettes and crisp incised contour lines softened by worn fresco edges, hairline cracks, and selective pigment loss
lighting: warm raking Mediterranean daylight with gentle stone-bounce illumination and subdued shadow contrast
subject_constraints: ancient Greek domestic and mythic visual vocabulary only: pithos jars, simple woven garments, stone or plaster interiors, wooden furnishings, olive branches, amphora and meander motifs, stylized personifications of escaping troubles, and symbolic hope represented through restrained light or a small remaining presence; consequences should spread visually through multiplying figures, shapes, or motifs rather than modern effects
historical_accuracy_note: Depict Pandora's original container as a large ancient Greek pithos or storage jar rather than a later European-style box. Avoid Roman armor, medieval objects, Renaissance architecture, modern locks, fantasy treasure chests, and other anachronisms. Clothing, vessels, furnishings, and decorative motifs should remain broadly consistent with archaic or early classical Greek visual culture while acknowledging that black-figure imagery is being used as an interpretive storytelling language rather than a literal reconstruction.
hero_rendering_in_world: If the protagonist appears beyond the opener, preserve his tall slim silhouette, chestnut hair shape, beard and moustache, green-sweater and dark-overalls identity, and rust-boot silhouette, but translate them into flattened fresco forms with black-figure-inspired contouring, muted mineral pigments, and lightly weathered plaster texture rather than redesigning him as an ancient Greek character.
negative_constraints: no photorealism, no glossy 3D CGI, no anime, no modern cinematic fantasy armor, no Renaissance oil-painting look, no neon effects, no polished marble-statue aesthetic, no literal magical smoke explosions, no European treasure chest as Pandora's container, no dense archaeological engraving texture, no blueprint or technical-diagram language
reason: Pandora's story has unusually strong affinity with an ancient Greek visual language, and the episode plan specifically points toward black-figure pottery, fresco, and aged-stone textures. A fresco-primary treatment provides a coherent full-frame world while black-figure conventions supply instantly recognizable Greek silhouettes and symbolic storytelling without forcing every scene into the narrow geometry of a vase. This is intentionally a new style because the operator directive forbids reuse, and it also improves between-episode diversity: the recent sequence already used ink wash, retro educational illustration, historical engraving on papyrus, and luminous technical drawing, so another paper-grain or diagrammatic treatment would feel repetitive.
